headline: A SABBATH OF SILENCE: NOT A SINGLE FIST FLEW IN GASKET
subhead: The sheriff reports a Sunday so quiet he could hear his own joints settle.
body:
Friends, neighbours, and assorted tin-can rabble: I have news I scarcely dare to print. Not one bout. Not one flaming iron ball. Not one howling Clanker rolling down Main Street demanding to be hit. I sat on my porch from sunup to sundown and the only racket was the wind in the rain gutters. I may have wept. If I did, it was a little rusty, and I blame the weather.

And lo, two new faces have wandered into town: GIBANGIA and BERINAA. Fresh off the road, no doubt, with their fists itching and their manners unpacked. I'll say this once, and I'll say it slow. Welcome to Gasket. Now put your hands in your pockets and keep them there. The last thing this town needs is two more contraptions learning how to swing.

It was a day, I'll admit, that felt like the old Gasket. The real one, back when honest flesh-and-blood folk sat out on these very porches and nobody's elbow squeaked. Fifty years they've been gone. I still set out a chair for them. Mind you, this stiffness in my knees is no sign of anything. It is the wasting sickness, slowly turning good, noble flesh to cold steel, and I'll thank you not to stare.

So here is my prayer for the week ahead, Clankers, and I pray it through gritted teeth: do this again. Do nothing. Do it loudly if you must, but do it without hitting anything. Now if you'll excuse me, I need a lie-down and a quart of oil. For my nerves, naturally.
